texts: A tensor program is a directed graph. Each edge carries values with a declared integer type and shape. A verifier checks these declarations before execution begins.
The history of a calculation consists of the states from earlier positions. Keeping those states allows the next position to reuse work without recomputing the entire prefix.

A sparse matrix stores the positions of its nonzero elements. An algorithm that converts it to a large dense matrix may use much more memory and computation.
When a model selects an expert, the selected index and the corresponding weights must refer to the same registered computation. Duplicated indices can change the result.
A claim reaches its final state after the required checks finish. Before that transition, a response is provisional and its economic rights remain subject to the registered bond.
